messages:
maya: Quick sync — after last night's outage I sketched a PRD delta + runbook updates we should ship before we re-open dedicated pools to Beta customers. Posting draft link: https://internal.redwood/prd/runbook-delta
jonathan: Skimmed it. 👍 Major ask: add an automatic downgrade/fallback policy for model variants when tail latency spikes. We need clear thresholds and acceptance tests.
devon: Agreed. Also we should add a safety circuit for KV cache eviction storms — that was the root cause last time. Edge case: cold-starts + long sequences caused memory pressure.
olivia: From SRE perspective: suggest three guardrails:
1) Circuit breaker: if 95th pct latency > 1200ms for 5m, route new requests to smaller model variant and reduce concurrency by 30%.
2) Canary rollout policy: 5% -> 20% -> 60% -> 100% with health checks at each step.
3) Emergency manual rollback + automated fallback to hosted pool if dedicated capacity fails continuous health checks for 3min.
maya: Nice clear wording. I'll add as requirements in the PRD. We also need runbook steps (who paged, what to toggle, where to check traces).
olivia: Draft runbook snippet (put this verbatim into the doc):
```
Runbook excerpt — Dedicated pool latency spike
1) Pager -> SRE oncall
2) Check /metrics/serving/latency  [95p, 99p]
3) If 95p > 1200ms for 5m: trigger fallback policy CLI:
   redwood infra fallback --pool dedicated --target hosted --reason latency_spike
4) Reduce dedicated concurrency: redwood infra config set --pool dedicated --concurrency 0.7x
5) Notify customers via status page and CS channel
```
jonathan: Two questions:
- Acceptance criteria for shipping this? e.g., unit tests + integration test that simulates spike and verifies fallback works within 90s.
- Who signs off on SLA change messaging to customers?
devon: For acceptance criteria propose:
- Automated integration test: simulate 95p latency >= 1200ms for 6m — fallback executes and routes 100% of new sessions to hosted within 120s.
- Canary must pass synthetic p95 and error-rate checks for 10m at each step.
- E2E smoke with customer workload (sample prompts) runs under canary and shows quality delta <= 5% as measured by eval set.
carlos: PM decision: prioritize the minimal delta for next patch (guardrails + runbook + automated fallback). Full KV eviction redesign is next quarter. We need to commit to ship the minimal set this sprint. :thumbsup:
maya: OK I'm updating the PRD to reflect that scope: "MVP: guardrails + runbook + automated downgrade + canary policy". I'll add acceptance criteria exactly as discussed and link the integration test harness.
sre-bot: scheduled-deploy: release/guardrails-mvp -> staging at 2026-04-10T03:00Z
olivia: One more edge case to add: network partition between control plane and dedicated hosts can delay health checks. Add a timeout: if control plane cannot confirm canary health for > 3m, treat as failed step and rollback.
devon: Add a small change to rollback behavior: when rolling back, also proactively clear KV caches on affected nodes to avoid repeated OOM loops. Command in runbook:
```
redwood infra kv-ops clear --selector pool=dedicated --age>1h
```
jonathan: I left inline comments in the doc about telemetry events we must emit so the console can show cost & latency delta per-route during fallback.
carlos: Good. Can legal/CS sign-off happen offline? CS needs canned customer messaging for SLA impact.
maya: I'll loop in @support_lead and @legal during docs review. Plan: ship guardrails + runbook by end of week, enable canary next week. If no objections, I'll convert draft to PRD change and assign owners.
olivia: No objections from SRE. We'll own the runbook operational steps and test harness.
jonathan: I'll own the integration tests + telemetry.
maya: Thanks all — I'll post the PRD delta PR shortly and ping reviewers. :rocket:
